370Z Track Data Analysis

Post-cooling-upgrade validation — 7/6 track day & 7/19 autocross, plus 2 weeks of street driving

Verdict at a glance

The headline on each of your concerns. Detail in the sections below.

Driving timeline — 12 days reconstructed

Clock was unreliable, so days were rebuilt from boot-counter order + cold-start thermal signatures. Bar = total drive minutes; color = intensity. The two intense days stand out.

Oil starvation check — the big one

If the VQ37 were starving in corners, pressure would crater at high rpm. It doesn't. Bands show pressure percentiles per rpm bin; the p5–p95 shaded band and the minimum-ever line are what matter.
Shaded = 5th–95th percentile of oil pressure in each rpm bin. Solid = median. Dashed red = the single lowest sample recorded in that bin. Above ~3,500 rpm the minimum never approaches a starvation zone.

Steering fluid overheating — confirmed

The 7/6 track day stitched together (7 hard sessions, gaps trimmed). Red line = 230°F critical (boil/foam-over), orange = 240°F. This is your tank overflow, in data.
Per hard session: peak fluid temp (bar) and seconds spent ≥230°F (label).
Track vs Autocross vs Street
Peak steering temp by day. Only sustained 30-min track sessions boil; short autocross runs get warm (223°F) but don't cross the line.

All systems — per-day heat map

Peak temperatures each day vs their critical thresholds (steer 230 · coolant 220 · trans 230 · diff 260 °F). Red = over critical, orange = within 15°.

Pick any logged session to see its traces. RPM on the left axis; temps & oil pressure on the right.
